proposals.title: Main skips crypto
proposals.why: In crypto the market scores a Brier of 0.034 against Jev+research's 0.117 (9 resolved), so any edge we think we see there is most likely our own error. This is an experiment on a small sample.
proposals.judge_by: On the yardstick, main's P&L on bets opened after this change is at least original's. Meanwhile, original's crypto bets over the same period lose money in total.
proposals.status_reason: main rules v2: skips none → crypto

proposals.title: Bold meets the info gate halfway
proposals.why: Bold's extra bets, where Jev's info rating is 0.2–0.5, are losing $31.79 per $100 (7 bets), and main's info-stopped markets lose $70 per $100 (16). A 0.35 threshold tests where the cutoff really belongs, without collapsing bold into a copy of main.
proposals.judge_by: Bold's P&L per $100 staked since the change beats its old -$31.79 per $100, and is closer to or above main's over the same period.

proposals.title: Claude direct, pickier and without crypto
proposals.why: Claude is our best forecaster (Brier 0.132 on 24) yet lost all 3 of its settled bets. The places where it disagrees with the market by only 8% are probably where the market is right. This challenger demands a 12% edge, skips crypto, and bets half as much per bet.
proposals.judge_by: Positive P&L, and more P&L per $100 staked than claude_direct over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: started automatically within the allowed bounds

proposals.title: Break results down by price paid
proposals.why: Many losses, including all 3 of claude_direct's and every info-gate-stopped group, show -$100 per $100, meaning the whole stake was lost. That pattern suggests we may be buying cheap longshots. A breakdown of wins and P&L by ask price (for example <0.2, 0.2–0.5, 0.5–0.8, >0.8), for placed and stopped bets, would let us set min_ask and max_ask from evidence instead of guessing.
proposals.judge_by: The review data includes a by-price breakdown, and within 2 reviews it leads to either a min_ask/max_ask tune or a clear finding that price doesn't matter.

proposals.title: Jev alone, bold: pickier, no crypto or economy
proposals.why: Jev alone scores worse than the market in every category, with a Brier of 0.221 against 0.052 in crypto (21 resolved) and 0.294 against 0.168 in economy (12 resolved). This strategy has lost $17 per $100 staked (22 bets, 6 settled). The experiment is to demand a bigger edge and skip Jev's worst categories, while leaving the info gate at 0.2 so it stays distinct from Jev alone.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, P&L per $100 staked beats its all-time -$17.4 per $100 and is at least as good as jev_alone over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: jev_alone_bold rules v2: edge bar 8% → 12%; skips none → crypto, economy

proposals.title: Jev + research, picky
proposals.why: Bets main actually placed have lost $15 per $100 (7 settled), and Jev + research trails the market badly in crypto and economy. This tests whether requiring a 15% edge, and dropping both categories, turns research-driven bets profitable. It can run now, while main is locked until tomorrow.
proposals.judge_by: P&L per $100 staked is at or above zero, and above original's on the markets both bet over the same period.

proposals.title: Paired Brier scores and a calibration sanity check
proposals.why: Each source is scored on a different set of markets (Claude on 33, the market on 120), so 'Claude beats the market' can't be trusted. The calibration map has a=1.489, and its forecasts score worse than raw Jev (0.236 against 0.199), even though reviews blame Jev being overconfident. A=1.489 may be stretching forecasts further from 50/50 instead of pulling them back.
proposals.judge_by: Joey approves, and the next review shows Brier scores for each source against the market on the same resolved markets, plus the calibrated source's score on markets the map wasn't fitted to.
proposals.status_reason: approved by Joey 2026-10-02; needs a code session

proposals.title: Score forecasters on 30c+ markets only
proposals.why: Since 2026-10-01 every strategy bets only at 30c or more, but the Brier table (market 0.114 vs our best 0.121) mixes in the long shots we no longer touch. We need to know whether any forecaster beats the price where we actually bet, matched market by market.
proposals.judge_by: The review data gains each source's Brier score next to the market's on the same resolved markets priced 30c or more. Success means Joey can see whether any source scores below the market there, which decides which challenger to start next.

proposals.title: Shrink forecasts toward the market before computing edge
proposals.why: The market's Brier (0.123, 201 markets) beats every forecaster, and most of our losses came from bets where we disagreed with it most, such as long shots that went 1 for 21. A strategy option that blends the forecast with the market price (for example 50/50) before the edge check would bet only where a disagreement survives that discount. The forecasters themselves would still never see the price.
proposals.judge_by: Replay the blended rule on resolved markets that were judged after the code ships, and compare it with the unblended rule on the same markets. It succeeds if settled P&L per $100 is higher and it has fewer losing bets.

proposals.title: Gate ledger and price breakdown for 30c+ markets only
proposals.why: The gate ledger mixes in long shots, which lost 1 in 42 before the floor. That makes every 'stopped by the info gate' number look worse than it would under today's rules: calibrated's info-stopped markets show −$7.1 per $100 (66) and main's −$24.6 (78). We can't sensibly tune the info gates until the ledger shows only markets the 30c floor would let through.
proposals.judge_by: The next reviews show a 30c+ gate ledger and a by_price_paid split for each strategy's since_change bets. It is worth having if it changes or confirms an info-gate decision once there is enough data.

proposals.title: Pooled tally of bets placed under the floor
proposals.why: Each strategy has 0–1 settled bets since 2026-10-01, so the floor's '30 settled bets' test will take weeks per strategy. Pooling every strategy's 30c+ bets placed since the floor, measured against original's long shots over the same period, would answer whether the floor pays much sooner.
proposals.judge_by: The review reports pooled P&L per $100 on 30c+ bets since 2026-10-01 alongside original's under-30c bets. The floor is confirmed if the pooled result beats original's long shots.

proposals.title: Retire ch6 (picky Jev + research)
proposals.why: ch6 has settled 2 bets, lost both, and is down $4.0k. Its idea is to bet only where Jev disagrees with the market by 15+ points, but the market out-forecasts Jev + research (0.150 vs 0.201 Brier over 191 shared markets). Two results are noise, so this is a judgment call: the slot is better spent on a different hypothesis.
proposals.judge_by: No later check: its 3 open bets settle and are recorded, and the slot goes to the challenger below.
proposals.status_reason: ch6 retired; its open bets still settle and its record stays on the page

proposals.title: Calibrated, favourites only
proposals.why: Across strategies, bets on favourites (60c and up) have gone 12 wins to 6 losses. The calibrated forecaster went 5 for 5 there (+$3.6k), and main 2 for 2 (+$1.4k). This tests whether calibrated Jev makes money when it only backs prices of 55c and above. It is an experiment on tiny numbers.
proposals.judge_by: P&L per $100 staked is positive, and better than the calibrated strategy's over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: started automatically within the allowed bounds

proposals.title: Bold skips crypto, like main
proposals.why: In crypto, Jev + research scores 0.151 against the market's 0.087 over 56 resolved markets. Bold is down $20.3k, the worst of any strategy, on 33 settled. Skipping crypto leaves bold differing from main only in its info gate (0.35 vs 0.5), which makes it a clean test of that gate.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, bold's P&L per $100 staked beats its current all-time -$22 per $100, and is within $10 per $100 of main's over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: bold rules v4: skips none → crypto
